events.text: The steppe wind blows for three days without stopping. Sand gets into the rice, the tea and your teeth.

effects.log: By the third day you can stand in it like a post. The garrison soldiers stop laughing.

choices.text: Sit it out with the soldiers

effects.log: Chess, sour wine and stories about the other side of the river.

events.text: Raiders cross the frozen river at night. The garrison bell rings, and everyone with a blade runs to the wall.

ok.log: The raiders pull back at dawn. The captain writes your name in his report.

fail.log: You hold, bleeding, until the reinforcements come.

choices.text: Get the villagers into the fort

effects.log: Forty families, one gate, no one left behind.

events.text: The border garrison holds an archery contest. The prize is a horse. The favourite is a sergeant with one eye.

ok.log: Your last arrow splits his. The horse is yours.

fail.log: The one-eyed sergeant wins, as he has for eleven years.

effects.log: He wins, and tips his arrow-carrier. (10 taels)

events.text: The Paeng family of the north throws a feast for a victory nobody remembers the details of. Everyone in town is invited.

effects.log: They are loud, generous and very hard to out-drink. You wake up on a roof.
You lose. He hugs you. Paeng hugs hurt more than their punches.

events.text: Nomad traders set up felt tents outside the border town, selling horses, furs and a cheese that could stop a sword.

effects.log: Your winters become survivable. (−12 taels)
It is sour, strong and alive. You feel invincible for a day.

events.text: A blizzard buries the northern pass. A merchant caravan is trapped on the far side, lights fading.

choices.text: Break a trail through the snow

ok.log: You reach them by midnight and lead them back one by one.

fail.log: The snow beats you. You barely crawl back.

choices.text: Keep the fires burning for them

effects.log: You feed the beacon fire all night so they can find the way. Most of them do.

events.text: An old soldier missing an arm teaches border children to fight with the one he has left.

effects.log: He is the best teacher you have ever had. He only needs one hand to knock you over.
He watches you chop and says: "You chop like someone who has never been cold." He is right.

events.text: Wolves come down from the hills in the hard winter and circle the sheep pens every night.

ok.log: The pack leader tests you once and decides the sheep are not worth it.

fail.log: A wolf takes a bite of your leg before the pack runs.

effects.log: Two days of cold carpentry. Not one sheep lost.

events.text: A travelling merchant in the border town asks a lot of questions about the garrison. He pays for every drink.

effects.log: The merchant is a spy. The captain gives you a reward and a warning to keep quiet.

choices.text: Eat his dinner and tell him nothing

effects.log: A free dinner, and only tea for you. He leaves disappointed.

events.text: Standing on the old wall at night, you can see the campfires of the nomads on the steppe, as many as the stars.

effects.log: You stop at three thousand. The wall has never felt so thin.
An old border song about going home. Every sentry knows it. Nobody finishes it without stopping.

events.text: The horse market of the north: a thousand horses, a thousand liars, and one very honest boy selling a skinny foal.

effects.log: In a year it is the fastest horse in town. The boy was honest. (−30 taels)
You learn more about lying in an hour than in your whole life.

events.text: Two northern swordsmen duel on a frozen lake at dawn, as their fathers did. The ice sings with every step.

effects.log: The duel ends when the ice does. Both come out cursing, alive and friends.

choices.text: Warn them the ice is thin

effects.log: They ignore you, then fall through. You pull them both out. They owe you a drink each.

events.text: A famous poet exiled to the frontier sits at the tavern, writing poems about home on the wall with his finger in wine.

effects.log: He writes a poem about you. It is not flattering. It becomes famous anyway.
He looks at the paper, then at you, and weeps. He writes on the paper, for once.

events.text: A brown sandstorm rolls in from the steppe. The sun turns orange and the whole town shutters itself.

effects.log: Three days of chess with the innkeeper. You win a pickle jar.
Sand in every part of you, and not one sheep lost.

events.text: A young deserter hides in your woodpile. He is sixteen and terrified of the war.

effects.log: He works your fields, eats your rice and leaves with a new name. Years later a letter comes.
He goes back. You hear he became a sergeant. You hope that was kindness.
